_doc: Battle 21 (George Washington) geodata for the 3D worlds. x, y = BASE frame units (washington/data/frame.json: web mercator z10, origin [75952, 98000], x east, y south; ~116 m/unit). A region of zoom z uses x * 2^(z-10). Built by washington/tools/make_geo.py from OSM lines + built-in 1776 points / roads + the research files (research/geo_brooklyn.json, geo_jersey.json) when present.

places.name: Brooklyn Ferry landing (Fulton Ferry), Brooklyn side
places.src: Neighbourhood centre per Wikipedia 'Fulton Ferry, Brooklyn' (40.70333,-73.99306); foot of Fulton St; historical marker at the landing says the army embarked here night of 29 Aug 1776; Johnston p.221 'the present Fulton Ferry'
places.note: Embarkation point of the evacuation (McDougall in charge). The 1776 shore was a little inland of today's Brooklyn Bridge Park piers; today's Fulton Ferry Landing is a good screen position.

places.name: Manhattan landing, Peck Slip (head of slip)
places.src: Modern street grid (Peck Slip / Water St); position reasoned, not surveyed. Manhattan terminus of the Brooklyn ferry is generally given as Peck Slip (verify: no source page fetched states it for 1776)
places.note: Landing area for the evacuation. Sources conflict or are silent on the exact Manhattan stairs; draw the landing as the stretch Peck Slip - Fly Market. The 1776 shoreline lay about at Water/Front St, roughly 100-220 m INLAND (west) of today's South St / FDR Drive (landfill since).

places.name: Fly Market (foot of Maiden Lane), Manhattan
places.src: Reasoned from Maiden Lane / Pearl-Water St grid; Johnston does not name it
places.note: Market and slip just SW of Peck Slip; the boats were ordered to the 'east harbor of the city' (Johnston p.216). Use as a secondary landing marker only if the landing is shown as a stretch.

places.name: Fort Putnam (hill, later Fort Greene), Brooklyn Heights line
places.src: Johnston pp.70-73 (hill of Washington/Fort Greene Park, 'salient point of the line'); Wikipedia 'Fort Greene Park' (park centre 40.6919,-73.9755; Prison Ship Martyrs' Monument stands on the hill)
places.note: Star fort, 4-5 guns, named for Rufus Putnam (Johnston). Smallwood's Marylanders held it on the night of the evacuation (Johnston p.222). Main target of the British approaches.

places.name: Fort Greene (1776 star fort, NOT today's park)
places.src: Johnston p.71: ~300 yd left of Fort Box, 'a short distance above Bond Street, between State and Schermerhorn'; modern grid, position derived
places.note: Largest of the Brooklyn works, 6 guns, Little's regiment garrison. Derived position, acc 300: map artist should fit to the Hessian/Ratzer 1766-67 map.

places.name: Oblong Redoubt
places.src: Johnston p.71: 'corner of De Kalb and Hudson avenues'; modern grid, derived
places.note: Small circular redoubt commanding the Jamaica/Flatbush road, centre of the line.

places.name: Redoubt on the Left (Cumberland St)
places.src: Johnston p.72: 'middle of the present Cumberland Street, midway between Willoughby and Myrtle'
places.note: Small work east of Fort Putnam; held by part of Hand's riflemen (Capt. Miller) on the evacuation night (Johnston p.222).

places.name: Fort Box (right end of the line)
places.src: Johnston pp.70-71: 'on or near the line of Pacific Street, a short distance above Bond'; Stiles 1776 sketch
places.note: Diamond-shaped, nearest Gowanus Creek; line continued from it to the marsh.

places.name: Fort Cobble Hill (Smith's barbette)
places.src: Johnston p.74: 'near the intersection of the present Court and Atlantic streets' (Punkiesberg); hill since cut away
places.note: 4 guns, interior position covering the rear / Red Hook peninsula.

places.name: Redoubt at the Mill (Gowanus mill dam)
places.src: Johnston p.75: 'near the corner of the present Degraw and Bond streets'
places.note: One-gun right-angle battery covering the mill-dam crossing of Gowanus Creek.

places.name: Fort Defiance, Red Hook (water battery)
places.src: Johnston p.75 (4 x 18-pdr barbette to stop ships passing east of Governors Island); position approximate, Red Hook shore much altered by landfill
places.note: The British ship Roebuck was 'the only ship that could fetch high enough' to exchange a few shots with it on 27 Aug (Admiral Howe, in Johnston p.217).

places.name: Fort Stirling (Columbia Heights, foot of Clark St)
places.src: Johnston pp.2-3 (bluff opposite the Coenties Battery, at about the foot of the present Clark St)
places.note: Heights battery facing Manhattan; Johnston: it could shell New York after the retreat. The unfinished citadel was near Henry and Pierrepont Sts (about 40.6954,-73.9928).

places.name: Governors Island (fort / batteries, 1776)
places.src: Johnston p.66 (Putnam occupied the island in April 1776); Fort Jay stands there today (Wikipedia coordinates for the island ~40.689,-74.017)
places.note: British men-of-war were moored just off its edge; its works helped close the harbour mouth to the East River.

places.name: Wallabout Bay (left end of the Brooklyn line)
places.src: Johnston p.73 / Montressor testimony 1779 ('lines constructed from Wallabout Bay')
places.note: Bay and swamp were filled in for the Brooklyn Navy Yard; the swamp 'at the edge of Wallabout Bay' anchored the left.

places.name: Gowanus Creek mouth (Gowanus Bay)
places.src: Modern Gowanus Canal geometry; creek was straightened into the canal 1860s
places.note: Right-hand flank water of the Brooklyn line; marsh and tidal creek.

places.name: Brouwer's Millpond crossing (Gowanus Creek, Stirling's escape)
places.src: Wikipedia 'Old Stone House (Brooklyn)': the SE branch of the canal ends ~400 m W of the house; pond ~80 yd wide
places.note: Where part of Stirling's men crossed the millpond on 27 Aug 1776.

places.name: Old Stone House (Vechte-Cortelyou House)
places.src: Wikipedia 'Old Stone House (Brooklyn)': 40.672958 N 73.984625 W, 336 3rd St, Washington Park (reconstructed 1934-35, original footprint)
places.note: Gist's ~260-270 Marylanders held the house vs 2,000+ British on 27 Aug. NOTE: '256 killed' is disputed (see FACT_NOTES).

places.name: Guan Heights - Battle Hill, Green-Wood
places.src: Johnston p.146: Martense Lane = southern boundary of Green-Wood; Battle Hill is the highest point of the ridge
places.note: Southern anchor of the Guan Heights line (Stirling vs Grant on the coast road below).

places.name: Red Lion Tavern (Gowanus Road)
places.src: Johnston p.146 ('about three miles from Brooklyn Church'); modern grid approximate
places.note: Coast-road position; Stirling's line held the Gowanus Road here.

places.name: Flatbush Pass / Battle Pass (Prospect Park)
places.src: Johnston p.156 note: breastwork 'now within the limits of Prospect Park ... across Battle Pass'
places.note: Centre of the Guan Heights line; Sullivan with Hessians (von Heister) in front. Approximate.

places.name: Bedford Pass
places.src: Johnston p.155: 3/4 mile left of the Flatbush road; held by Wyllys's and Chester's Connecticut regiments
places.note: Approximate (Bedford Ave / Eastern Pkwy area).

places.name: Jamaica Pass
places.src: Johnston p.155 ('about four miles from the fortified line'); Wikipedia 'Jamaica Pass' (no coordinates; area East New York 40.67,-73.89)
places.note: Northernmost pass, guarded by five militia officers on patrol (captured ~2-3 a.m. 27 Aug); Howe's night flank march came through it.

places.name: Howard's Halfway House (Jamaica Road tavern)
places.src: Johnston p.171: British column halted 'directly in front of Howard's Halfway House' SE of the pass
places.note: Approximate: Jamaica Ave near Cypress Hills.

places.name: Gravesend landing (British, 22 Aug 1776)
places.src: Johnston p.139-140 (Gravesend Bay, a mile east of the Narrows); Wikipedia 'Battle of Long Island' (04:00-08:00 landing, 15,000 ashore by noon)
places.note: Unopposed landing; frigates Phoenix, Greyhound, Rose + bomb ketches covered it.

places.name: Flatlands (British camp before the flank march)
places.src: Johnston p.170 (march from Flatlands via Shoemaker's Bridge to the Jamaica Road)
places.note: Starting point of Howe's night column, left ~21:00 on 26 Aug (Wikipedia).

places.name: The Narrows (Verrazzano passage)
places.note: British fleet entered 2 July and anchored in the Narrows / off Staten Island.

places.name: Staten Island, British landing area (Watering Place / Stapleton shore)
places.src: Wikipedia 'New York and New Jersey campaign' (landed unopposed 2-3 July 1776); Johnston p.94 (camps 'opposite' the Long Island heights)
places.note: Approximate; Howe's headquarters at Will Hicks's mansion (Johnston note). Hessians camped on the island after 12 Aug.

places.name: Fort Washington (Manhattan)
places.src: Wikipedia 'Battle of Fort Washington' (40.85278 N 73.93806 W)
places.note: Fell 16 Nov 1776; 2,837 prisoners (Wikipedia, Battlefields Trust).

places.name: Fort Lee (New Jersey)
places.note: Evacuated 20 Nov 1776 as 5,000 British/Hessians landed (Morris County NJ; Battlefields Trust: garrison ~2,000).

places.name: Kip's Bay landing (1776 shore, E 34th St)
places.src: Wikipedia/Battlefields Trust: ~12,000 landed 15 Sep 1776; 1776 shore lay inland (~First Ave) of today's FDR Drive
places.note: Approximate.

places.name: Harlem Heights (battle 16 Sep 1776)
places.src: Mount Vernon / Battlefields Trust (Morningside Heights, 'Hollow Way' near today's 120th St)
places.note: Approximate.

places.name: White Plains / Chatterton Hill (battle 28 Oct 1776)
places.src: Battlefields Trust: ~13,000 British/Hessians attacked 28 Oct; village centre is 41.034,-73.763
places.note: Approximate; the hill lies south of the village centre.

places.name: Hackensack, NJ
places.note: Washington's army passed here 21 Nov (to verify date).

places.name: Acquackanonk (Passaic), NJ
places.note: Bridge over the Passaic; army passed ~21-22 Nov (verify).

places.name: Newark, NJ
places.note: Washington left Newark 27 Nov (search result, to verify).

places.name: Elizabeth Town, NJ
places.note: On the retreat route.

places.name: Perth Amboy, NJ
places.note: British-held port later; used on the wide map.

places.name: New Brunswick, NJ (Raritan crossing)
places.note: Army reached the Raritan ~29 Nov; crossed and burned the bridge 1 Dec (search result, to verify).

places.name: Princeton, NJ
places.note: Retreat route; army ~2 Dec.

places.name: Trenton, NJ
places.note: Army crossed the Delaware here and above 2-8 Dec; Howe/Cornwallis entered 8 Dec.

places.name: McConkey's Ferry (Pennsylvania side, Washington Crossing)
places.src: Washington Crossing Historic Park (McConkey's Ferry Inn)
places.note: Army camped near it in Dec; the Christmas crossing started here (outside this film part).

places.name: Morristown, NJ
places.note: Winter quarters Jan 1777 (outside this part; for the wide map).

places.name: Philadelphia
places.note: Congress fled 12 Dec 1776.

places.name: Baltimore (Henry Fite's house)
places.note: Congress reconvened here 20 Dec 1776 (Maryland State Archives; history.state.gov).

places.name: McConkey's Ferry landing (Pennsylvania side)
places.src: Derived: Johnson Ferry House (NJ) at 40.2993,-74.8682 per OSM + river ~275 m wide (ABT: ~300 yd) + Washington Crossing Bridge ~40.2986,-74.872; NOT surveyed
places.note: Army embarked here from about 5-6 p.m. on 25 Dec 1776 (ATL; WP). Washington Crossing Historic Park (PA). River flows SE. Use as the departure point; snap to the real bank in the basemap.

places.name: Johnson's Ferry landing (New Jersey side)
places.src: Derived from OSM Johnson Ferry House 40.2993,-74.8682 (river bank ~350 m west); NOT surveyed
places.note: Landing on the NJ shore; guns over by ~3 a.m., march began ~4 a.m. 26 Dec (ATL; WP). Washington Crossing State Park.

places.name: Johnson Ferry House (NJ, modern museum)
places.note: Reference point only; do not draw the modern house.

places.name: Bear Tavern (hamlet, Bear Tavern Rd / Pennington-Titusville Rd)
places.src: OSM Nominatim point (this session) 'Pennington-Titusville Road, Bear Tavern, Hopewell Twp'
places.note: Fischer's 'Bear Tavern road' is the first road inland from the landing. The hamlet name in OSM lies NE of the landing; the 1776 tavern location is uncertain (acc 600 m).

places.name: Birmingham (road fork where the army split)
places.src: Approx. from OSM Bear Tavern Rd (40.2765,-74.8278) and Scotch Rd (40.2839,-74.8062); location of 1776 Birmingham crossroads NOT verified (acc 800 m); Fischer/Stryker maps needed
places.note: Greene's column (with Washington) took the Scotch and Pennington Roads; Sullivan's took the River Road (WP).

places.name: Pennington Road outpost (Wiederholdt's cooper-shop picket)
places.src: WP: outpost at a cooper shop on Pennington Road ~1 mile NW of Trenton; position from OSM Pennington Ave 40.2387,-74.7749
places.note: 1 officer + 24 men under Lt. Andreas Wiederholdt (Bloomsburg plan, WP). First contact ~8 a.m. 26 Dec.

places.name: Trenton Battle Monument (head of King and Queen Streets; Knox's guns)
places.note: Monument marks the head of King (now N. Warren) and Queen (now N. Broad) Streets where the American guns were set up (WP). Draw the 1776 street grid, not the monument.

places.name: King Street (N. Warren St) - head
places.src: OSM Nominatim point (this session) N Warren/Battle Monument
places.note: King St ran N-S through 1776 Trenton; Knox oversaw the guns here.

places.name: King Street (N. Warren St) - foot at the Assunpink
places.note: Foot of King St at the creek.

places.name: Queen Street (N. Broad St) - head
places.src: OSM Nominatim point (this session) N Broad St 40.2247,-74.7645
places.note: Queen St = today's N. Broad St.

places.name: Queen Street (N. Broad St) - foot / Assunpink bridge
places.src: OSM S Broad St 40.2182,-74.7642; Assunpink Dr 40.2175,-74.7649
places.note: The Assunpink bridge ('the bridge') on Queen St: Sullivan blocked it on 26 Dec so the Hessians could not flee; the American line held it on 2 Jan (WP).

places.name: Old Barracks (Trenton)
places.note: Surviving 1758 barracks; British/Hessian quarters in 1776, west edge of the town near the river.

places.name: Rall's headquarters (Stacy Potts house, King St)
places.src: Approx. only: house stood on King St in the town centre (Stryker/Fischer) - exact site NOT verified
places.note: Some accounts put the HQ at merchant Abraham Hunt's house instead (see FACT_NOTES B2/B6). Rall was carried here after being wounded and died here that night.

places.name: Hessian main posts (Rall + Lossberg quarters, north half of town)
places.src: Approx. from americanwars.org ch. VIII/WP order of battle: Rall and Lossberg regiments quartered in northern Trenton
places.note: Both regiments formed in King and Queen Streets and were swept by the guns at the head of the streets.

places.name: Knyphausen regiment quarters (south, by the Assunpink bridge)
places.src: Approx. from americanwars.org ch. VIII: Knyphausen regiment in the south on both sides of the bridge
places.note: Regiment marched the wrong way and surrendered separately (WP). Acting commander Major von Dechow mortally wounded.

places.name: Mill Hill (rise north of the Assunpink)
places.src: OSM Nominatim point (this session) Mill Hill Park
places.note: 2 Jan 1777: American guns and the line covered the bridge from the south bank; British formed on the north side around Mill Hill.

places.name: Trenton Ferry / lower ferry (Ewing's planned crossing)
places.src: Approx.: OSM Calhoun Street Bridge 40.2199,-74.7781 near the old lower ferry; location NOT verified
places.note: Gen. James Ewing (~700 Pa. militia) was to cross here and hold the Assunpink bridge; ice stopped him (WP).

places.name: Bordentown (Donop's Hessian post)
places.note: Donop commanded two Hessian brigades from here; Cadwalader's planned diversion (WP/ATL).

places.name: Bristol / Dunk's Ferry (Cadwalader's crossing, PA side)
places.src: Approx.: OSM Bristol borough 40.0954,-74.8577; Dunks Ferry Rd Bensalem 40.0993,-74.9504 - actual ferry landing NOT verified
places.note: Cadwalader crossed some men, recalled them when guns could not land (WP). Dunk's Ferry is a few miles upstream of Bristol toward Bordentown's opposite shore.

places.name: Burlington, NJ (baggage sent here 2-3 Jan)
places.src: OSM Nominatim point (this session) Burlington City
places.note: FACT_NOTES G3: baggage sent to Burlington `[K]`.

places.name: Five Mile Run (Hand's first stand 2 Jan)
places.src: Approx. only: name used by WP; ~5 miles from Trenton on the Princeton Post Road near Lawrence Twp (Brunswick Pike 40.2478,-74.7391; Princeton Pike 40.2859,-74.7132). NOT verified
places.note: Hand's riflemen gave up this stream first.

places.name: Shabakunk Creek (Hand's second stand)
places.src: OSM Nominatim point (this session) Shabakunk Creek, Lawrence Twp
places.note: Hand held the wooded south bank and fired at close range (WP). ~3 miles from Trenton.

places.name: Stockton Hollow (final delay, ~0.5 mi from town)
places.src: Approx.: WP says 'roughly half a mile from Trenton' on the Post Road north of town; NOT verified
places.note: British reached it ~3 p.m.; Hand's men then fell back into the town fighting from houses (WP). 6-10 US killed/wounded (Peckham).

places.name: Maidenhead (modern Lawrenceville)
places.src: OSM Nominatim point (this session) Main Street, Lawrenceville
places.note: Leslie's rearguard (~1,200-1,500) and, 29 Dec, the Black Watch camped here (Princeton Forbes finding aid; WP).

places.name: Sandtown (road east of Trenton used on the night march)
places.src: Approx. only: OSM 'Mercerville, Hamilton Twp'; the Sand Town Rd position is NOT verified
places.note: Night march 2-3 Jan: Trenton - Sandtown - Quaker Bridge - Quaker Road (ABT; WP).

places.name: Quaker Bridge (Assunpink crossing on Quaker Bridge Rd)
places.src: Approx.: OSM Quaker Bridge Rd 40.2766,-74.6695 north end; actual bridge over the Assunpink NOT verified
places.note: WP: army moved on Quaker Bridge Road in what is now Hamilton Twp by 2 a.m.

places.name: Quaker Road / Sawmill Road turn (disused farm lane to Clarke's)
places.src: OSM Quaker Road, Battlefield Area, Princeton 40.3315,-74.6811; ABT: 'Quaker Road, then a disused farm lane (Sawmill Road)'
places.note: Army left the Post Road here to approach Princeton from the south and avoid the fortified King's Highway (ABT).

places.name: Stony Brook bridge (Worth's Mill, Post Road)
places.src: OSM 'Stony Brook Bridge, Lawrenceville Road, Battlefield Area, Princeton'
places.note: Mercer's column was ordered to break the bridge; British column from Princeton crossed toward Maidenhead here (WP; ABT).

places.name: Thomas Clarke house (Princeton Battlefield)
places.src: Approx. from OSM Princeton Battlefield State Park 40.3308,-74.6748 / Mercer Oak 40.3316,-74.6755; house position NOT verified
places.note: Washington's army crossed Thomas Clarke's farm land before the clash; Mercer was treated here and died 12 Jan (ABT/WP).

places.name: William Clarke's orchard / Mercer Oak (Mercer vs Mawhood)
places.src: OSM Nominatim point (this session) Mercer Oak
places.note: Mercer's brigade (~300) met Mawhood's 17th Foot here; bayonet charge, Mercer mortally wounded (WP/ABT).

places.name: Frog Hollow (ravine S of Princeton)
places.src: Approx. only (name from Princeton Battlefield Society maps); position NOT verified
places.note: The 40th and 55th fell back across this ravine toward Nassau Hall.

places.name: Nassau Hall (Princeton)
places.note: British 40th/55th survivors held out here; 194 surrendered after Hamilton's guns and the door was broken (WP).

places.name: Kingston (NJ)
places.note: Washington's column turned north to Kingston after Princeton, rather than fall on New Brunswick (ABT; WP).

places.name: Somerset Court House (Millstone)
places.note: Army reached it the night of 3 Jan; Pluckemin 5 Jan (WP).

places.name: Pluckemin
places.src: Approx. only; NOT verified (WP: army at Pluckemin by 5 Jan)

places.name: Morristown (Morristown Green)
places.note: Winter quarters; army arrived the evening of 6 Jan 1777 (WP; ABT says 5 Jan).

places.name: New Brunswick (British post; stayed British)
places.src: Approx.: modern city centre 40.486N,-74.452W (NOT from this session's queries)
places.note: British kept New Brunswick and Perth Amboy after Princeton (FACT_NOTES I2).

places.name: Perth Amboy (British post; stayed British)
places.src: Approx.: modern city 40.507N,-74.265W (NOT from this session's queries)
places.note: Ditto.

rivers.note: Freeke's mill pond at the head; the retreat of 27 Aug crossed it near the mouth

rivers.src: APPROXIMATE, drawn from OSM anchors (Johnson Ferry House, Calhoun St Bridge, Bordentown, Wilburtha) - NOT NHD; snap to NHD in the basemap (acc ~500 m). River ~300 yd wide at the crossing (ABT).

rivers.src: APPROXIMATE: anchored on OSM Assunpink Dr 40.2175,-74.7649 and S Broad St 40.2182,-74.7642 only; east and west ends are guesses (acc ~300 m). Snap to NHD.

works.note: south bank of the Assunpink from the Delaware past the bridge and Mill Hill upstream (~3 mi of fords); guns at the bridge

works.name: Brooklyn Heights fortified line, Wallabout swamp -> Gowanus marsh
works.src: Johnston 1878 'The Campaign of 1776 around New York and Brooklyn' (archive.org campaignof1776ar00john; Gutenberg 21990) pp.70-75; Montressor testimony 1779 ('about a mile and a half in extent', chain of five redoubts/forts); NOTE: points derived from street names, acc 250-400 m
works.note: Points run from the Wallabout swamp (NE end, the American left) to the Gowanus marsh (SW end, the American right): swamp, redoubt on the left, Fort Putnam, Oblong Redoubt, Fort Greene, Fort Box, marsh. Ditches, abatis, sally-ports; about 1.5 miles (2.4 km) long.

works.name: American line along the Assunpink south bank, 2 Jan 1777 (~3 miles)
works.src: APPROXIMATE: WP says line ~3 miles along the south bank; the fords at the east end (Sandtown road) uncertain (acc ~400 m). Bridge guns at ~40.2160,-74.7641.

moves.name: British siege parallel (night 28-29 Aug), schematic
moves.src: Johnston 1878 'The Campaign of 1776 around New York and Brooklyn' (archive.org campaignof1776ar00john; Gutenberg 21990) p.215: Little reports a parallel 60 rods (~300 m) long, 150 rods (~750 m) from Fort Putnam; Gordon: 400-500 yd from the redoubt on the left; position derived, acc 400
moves.note: Direction: SE of Fort Putnam. Howe chose regular approaches instead of storming (Johnston, Wikipedia).

moves.name: British flank march 26-27 Aug: Flatlands -> Shoemaker's Bridge -> Howard's -> Jamaica Pass -> Bedford
moves.src: Johnston 1878 'The Campaign of 1776 around New York and Brooklyn' (archive.org campaignof1776ar00john; Gutenberg 21990) pp.170-172; Wikipedia 'Battle of Long Island' (left 21:00, ~10,000 men, three Loyalist guides); positions approx acc 600
moves.note: Dawn 27 Aug the column rested beyond the pass; signal guns 09:00 for the frontal attack.

moves.name: Guan Heights line, schematic (Red Lion/Green-Wood -> Battle Pass -> Bedford Pass -> Jamaica Pass)
moves.src: Johnston 1878 'The Campaign of 1776 around New York and Brooklyn' (archive.org campaignof1776ar00john; Gutenberg 21990) pp.146-156
moves.note: Passes weakly held; Jamaica Pass by five patrol officers only.

moves.name: Evacuation boat track, Brooklyn Ferry -> Manhattan (night 29-30 Aug)
moves.src: Johnston 1878 'The Campaign of 1776 around New York and Brooklyn' (archive.org campaignof1776ar00john; Gutenberg 21990) pp.216-224
moves.note: East River ~ 0.7 mi (1.1 km) wide here; ~9,000 men in about 9-11 hours; last boats left Brooklyn after the fog rose, ~06:00-07:00 (sources 6 a.m. HistoryNet; 'before seven' Johnston).

moves.name: Manhattan shoreline of the East River, 1776 approximation (Whitehall -> Catharine Slip)
moves.src: Reasoned from the modern slips (Old Slip, Fly Market/Maiden Lane, Peck Slip, Catharine Slip); 1776 shore ~ Water/Front St, ~100-220 m inland of today's FDR Drive. acc 150-250 m. Verify against Ratzer map 1766-67.
moves.note: Water drawn east of this line; the modern South St is landfill.

moves.name: Brooklyn shoreline of the East River, 1776 approximation (Red Hook -> Wallabout)
moves.src: Reasoned from modern Furman St/Brooklyn Bridge Park; 1776 shore ~ Water/Columbia St side; acc 200-300 m; Red Hook/Wallabout heavily filled since
moves.note: Wallabout Bay is the last point; bay filled for the Navy Yard.

moves.name: American retreat route, Fort Lee -> Delaware (20 Nov - 8 Dec 1776), schematic
moves.src: Morris County NJ (route towns: Hackensack, Newark, Elizabeth, Woodbridge, New Brunswick, Princeton, Trenton); Wikipedia/NJ Military Museum (Delaware crossed 7-8 Dec); exact dates per town to verify (Fischer / McCullough)
moves.note: End point just across the Delaware at the Trenton ferries (Pennsylvania bank); boats from ~70 miles of river reported moved to the west bank (see FACT_NOTES, unverified figure).

moves.name: Greene's column (with Washington): landing - Bear Tavern Rd - Birmingham - Scotch Rd - Pennington Rd - Trenton (26 Dec)
moves.src: OSM anchors: Bear Tavern Rd (40.2765,-74.8278), Pennington Rd Ewing (40.2605,-74.7803), Pennington Ave (40.2387,-74.7749), Battle Monument; the Birmingham-to-Pennington Rd leg is interpolated (acc 700 m). WP: Greene took Scotch and Pennington Roads from the north.

moves.name: Sullivan's column: landing - River Road - Trenton (26 Dec)
moves.src: Anchors: OSM River Rd Wilburtha 40.2464,-74.8328, Calhoun Street Bridge 40.2199,-74.7781, Assunpink bridge. WP: Sullivan took River Road from the south and blocked the Assunpink crossing. Interpolated legs acc ~700 m.

moves.name: British advance: Princeton Post Road to Trenton (2 Jan)
moves.src: Post Road (King's Highway) Princeton-Maidenhead-Trenton; anchors OSM Stony Brook Bridge, Lawrenceville Main St, Brunswick Pike 40.2478,-74.7391; intermediate legs interpolated (acc ~800 m).

moves.name: Washington's night march 2-3 Jan: Trenton - Sandtown - Quaker Bridge - Quaker Rd - Sawmill Rd (~12 mi)
moves.src: Anchors: OSM Mercerville, Quaker Bridge Rd (40.2766,-74.6695), Quaker Rd Battlefield Area (40.3315,-74.6811); the first legs from Trenton and the Sandtown road are interpolated (acc ~1,000 m). ABT/WP: on the road by 2 a.m., Quaker Road then Sawmill Road, ~12 miles.

moves.name: Mercer's brigade toward the Stony Brook bridge, then the orchard (3 Jan)
moves.src: WP: Mercer sent to destroy the Stony Brook bridge; later in William Clarke's orchard; geometry interpolated (acc 200 m).

moves.name: Mawhood's advance from Princeton toward Maidenhead / Mercer (3 Jan)
moves.src: WP/MV: Mawhood had marched toward Trenton with 17th and 55th; turned them back on seeing Mercer. Interpolated (acc 400 m).
